output.description: Trust Fabric is bought by large enterprises and regulated organisations - spanning SaaS, online retail, fintech, automotive, energy, pharma, gaming, media, travel, telecoms and public sector - that run production Kubernetes with distributed, many-service architectures managed by an in-house engineering team. These buyers are based in North America, the UK and Ireland, or Continental Europe, and range from roughly 501 employees up to large global enterprises of around 50,000 staff. The purchase is decided by the platform, infrastructure or security leader who owns the cluster and its certificate estate, typically the CTO, CIO, CISO or a VP, Director or Head of Engineering, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, SRE, DevOps or Security.

seller.competitorTest: A competitor in the certificate-lifecycle management space sells to enterprise security and PKI teams who need to automate certificate issuance and renewal, regardless of whether their infrastructure runs on Kubernetes at scale.

buyer.rubric: Buyers are the platform, infrastructure or security leader who owns the Kubernetes cluster and its certificate estate: CTO, CIO, CISO, and the VP, Director or Head of Engineering, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Security Engineering, Information Security or Architecture, with the CEO qualifying only at companies under about 1,000 employees. Titles that carry a senior title but never buy this include the CFO, CMO, CRO, VP of Sales, VP of Marketing, and other commercial, HR or finance leaders.

requirements.text: The company runs production Kubernetes with a distributed architecture or many independent services.

The company operates its own infrastructure with an in-house engineering team rather than being an outsourced platform, MSP, systems integrator, consultancy, agency, private equity firm, recruiter, freelancer, or certificate-lifecycle vendor such as AppViewX, Entrust or CyberArk.
The company has between 501 and 50,000 employees.
The company's operations are uptime-critical or regulated such that an hour of downtime would be a board-level event.
The company is based in North America, the UK and Ireland, or Continental Europe.

The company shows a live buying signal such as a platform, SRE, infrastructure or PKI role posted in the last 30 days naming Kubernetes, TLS, mTLS, cert-manager, PKI or service mesh; public evidence of production Kubernetes at scale; a published SLA; DORA, PSD2, NIS2 or PCI DSS obligations; a new platform or security leader appointed in the last 12 months; a post-quantum commitment; or a public certificate or TLS incident in the last 90 days.

seller.description: Form3 operates a cloud-native, real-time account-to-account (A2A) payments platform, delivered as a managed service to banks and fintechs, providing access to domestic and international payment schemes across the US, UK and Europe via a single API.

icp.offer: Trust Fabric, a product installed into a Kubernetes cluster to manage certificate trust and infrastructure risk across distributed services; this excludes Form3's payments platform, which is out of scope for this profile.
icp.buyer: The platform, infrastructure or security leader who owns the cluster and its certificate estate: CTO, CIO, CISO, and the VP, Director or Head of Engineering, Platform Engineering, Infrastructure, Cloud, Site Reliability Engineering, DevOps, Security Engineering, Information Security or Architecture. CEO only at companies under about 1,000 people. Never the payments or commercial function. Excludes recruiters, HR, sales, marketing, individual engineers and academics. At most three people per company.

allOf.text: Runs production Kubernetes with a distributed architecture or many independent services (no cluster, no deal)
An in-house engineering team operates that infrastructure, not an outsourced platform
Uptime-critical or regulated, where an hour of downtime is a board-level event
Based in North America, the UK and Ireland, or Continental Europe
Not a consultant, agency, non-profit, private equity firm, recruiter, freelancer, managed service provider, systems integrator, or certificate-lifecycle vendor such as AppViewX, Entrust, or CyberArk
A platform, SRE, infrastructure or PKI role posted naming Kubernetes, TLS, mTLS, cert-manager, PKI or a service mesh
Public evidence of production Kubernetes at scale
DORA, PSD2, NIS2 or PCI DSS obligations
A new platform or security leader
A public certificate or TLS incident

output.description: Aris Search sells to managed service providers (MSPs) across the United States that deliver outsourced IT support—helpdesk, cloud, network, security, and project engineering—to their own clients, typically ranging from small owner-run shops up to larger regional roll-ups (roughly 1 to 150 employees per site). The buyer is the person who owns the decision to engage an outside recruiter for technical hires or who owns the technical headcount those hires fill—owners, founders, service-delivery and operations leaders, or HR/talent-acquisition leads. These MSPs are found nationwide, with the seller noting particular strength in Chicago and Dallas markets.

seller.competitorTest: A competitor in this space typically sells generalist IT recruiting services to any technology company, regardless of whether that company itself delivers managed services to outside clients.

buyer.rubric: Owners, founders, CEOs, presidents, COOs, and VPs/directors of service delivery, operations, managed services, or professional services at MSPs own this recruiting decision, as do heads of HR, recruiting managers, and directors of talent acquisition who own the recruiter relationship; market/regional presidents at roll-ups also own regional hiring. CFOs, controllers, VP/directors of sales or marketing, CTOs/CIOs at larger MSPs, security-delivery roles like CISO/vCISO, board members, and PE-parent executives carry senior titles but do not buy this.

requirements.text: The company must operate as a managed service provider (MSP) delivering outsourced IT support to its own clients.
The company must have between 1 and 150 employees.
The company must not itself be an IT staffing or recruiting firm.
The company must be based in the United States.
There is a dated situation, signal, or trigger indicating the company is actively hiring or expanding its technical or service-delivery staff.

seller.description: Aris Search is a recruiting/staffing firm that places IT and sales talent, including technicians and service-delivery staff (helpdesk, cloud, network, security, project engineers, service-delivery leads) at managed service providers (MSPs), across industries such as MSPs, IT solutions firms, SaaS, healthcare, finance, manufacturing, engineering, accounting, entertainment, logistics and industrial sectors.

icp.offer: Recruiting/placement services for technicians and service-delivery staff (helpdesk, cloud, network, security, project engineers, service-delivery leads) at managed service providers (MSPs) — i.e., engaging an outside recruiter for technical hiring.
icp.buyer: The person who owns the decision to engage an outside recruiter for technical hiring, or who owns the headcount those hires fill. POSITIVE: Owner, founder, CEO, president, managing partner (at an MSP under ~150 people, the owner usually makes this call personally); COO, chief services officer, chief customer officer, VP/director of service delivery, VP/director of operations, VP/director of managed services, VP/director of professional services; head of people, HR director, VP people, director of talent acquisition, recruiting manager (at small MSPs an 'HR Manager' who is the only HR person counts); market president/regional president at a roll-up (owns a regional P&L and its hiring). INFLUENCER (not positive): service desk manager, NOC manager, engineering manager, team lead; CTO/CIO at an MSP — labeled INFLUENCER unless the company is small enough that the CTO is a founder. HARD NEGATIVE: CFO, controller, finance director; VP/director of sales, account executives, account managers, marketing; CISO/vCISO delivering security to clients; individual engineers, technicians, analysts, project managers, consultants; board members, investors, advisors; anyone at a parent PE firm rather than at the MSP itself.

allOf.text: Company is a managed service provider (MSP)
Buyer is employed at the MSP itself, not at a parent PE firm

unknowns: The note's exception that a CTO/CIO counts as positive 'if the company is small enough that the CTO is a founder' does not define a precise size threshold, leaving ambiguity for borderline cases.
The '~150 people' threshold for owner/founder decision authority is approximate and not a hard cutoff, so companies near that size are ambiguous.
